about: Exercise library for Long Life Lifts rotation (the athlete, Oct 24, 2026: the coach proposes exercise swaps when a training block starts; the athlete accepts or keeps). One row per exercise with a stable id: every logged set is stored under this id (coach/strength_log.csv exercise_id), so an exercise that leaves the routine and comes back later keeps its whole history. pattern = the movement slot it can fill (a swap keeps the pattern, dose and time); favors = what it carries over to (bike, run, trail = climbing and descending, swim, health); why = one line for the proposal; the dose fields (sets, lo, hi, unit, load, per_side, step, next_hard, extra, legs) are copied into coach/strength.json when the exercise is swapped in. Equipment is what the athlete has at home: dumbbells, kettlebells, bench, pull-up bar, bands, a box or step. cautions name the stop signals that matter for it.

rows.name: Pistol squat
rows.why: Single-leg strength, balance and ankle control in one move; a warm-up that loads the stance leg.
rows.next_hard: box → floor → balance platform, then hold a DB

rows.name: Slow step-down (4 s down)
rows.why: Slow lowering off a step trains the quads and knee control for long descents (eccentric load).
rows.cautions: knee pain at the front of the knee: lower step

rows.name: Single-leg pogo hops
rows.why: Short, stiff ankle hops build the spring that running economy depends on.

rows.name: 2 s pause front squat
rows.why: Upright, quad-led squat with a pause at the bottom: the knee and hip angles and the push of the bike's power stroke.

rows.name: DB walking lunge
rows.why: One leg at a time in a moving stance: hip and knee stability and glute work close to running and hiking.
rows.cautions: ankle above a niggle: switch to reverse lunges in place

rows.name: Rear-foot-elevated split squat
rows.why: The heaviest single-leg squat you can load with dumbbells: quads and glutes for climbing, without a heavy bar.

rows.name: Goblet squat
rows.why: The simplest loaded squat; a light-week or restart option.

rows.name: Weighted pull-up
rows.why: Vertical pull for the swim catch and posture.

rows.name: One-arm DB row
rows.why: Horizontal pull with an anti-rotation hold; easier on the elbow than pull-ups.
rows.cautions: the option when the elbow aches on pull-ups

rows.name: DB Romanian deadlift
rows.why: Both-leg hinge: hamstrings, glutes and back strength with a load you can progress.

rows.name: Single-leg DB Romanian deadlift
rows.why: One-leg hinge: hip stability and glute control in the stance that running asks for; heavy enough with home dumbbells.

rows.name: Single-leg hip thrust (back on bench)
rows.why: Direct glute work at full hip extension; low back load.

rows.name: Incline DB bench
rows.why: Upper-body push for balance with the pulls.

rows.name: Push-up (feet raised when easy)
rows.why: Push with a moving shoulder blade; no bench needed.
rows.next_hard: feet on the bench, then a backpack

rows.name: Band face pulls
rows.why: Rear shoulder and upper back for posture on the bike and in the water.

rows.name: Band Y-T-W
rows.why: Lower trap and rotator cuff for the overhead swim stroke.

rows.name: Single-leg DB calf raise
rows.why: Calf and Achilles capacity for running mileage.

rows.name: Slow calf drop off a step (3 s down)
rows.why: Slow lowering loads the Achilles for downhills and long runs.
rows.cautions: ankle above a niggle: both legs, no load

rows.name: Side plank
rows.why: Lateral trunk and hip control for a steady pelvis on the run.
rows.next_hard: Copenhagen plank, knee on the bench

rows.name: Suitcase carry (one heavy DB)
rows.why: Walking with one heavy weight: trunk and hip stability under load, like a pack on a climb.

rows.name: Dead bug
rows.why: Front trunk control with a still low back, the position that holds the aero bars.
